newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds remain on the defensive.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds remain on the defensive.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed higher after some large sell-orders late in the session took futures through support, amid some disappointment over today's T-bond tender result.
Australian bond yields closed higher after some large sell-orders late in the session took futures through support, and amid some disappointment over today's T-bond tender result.
Traders said the market was also showing caution ahead several key U.S. economic indicators this week, which kicks off later today with the release of the September quarter employment cost index.
The main focus for the day was the A$800 million bond tender, which included the debut offering of A$600 million in the September 2009 stock.
"There was reasonable demand for the 2009. But there was never going to natural buyers of it because of the length of it. The real disappointment was in the 2002's," one trader said.

A$200 million was also tendered in the March 2002 bond which had been expected to draw a strong bid, but with all eyes on the performance of the 2009, the range of accepted bids was a wide seven basis points.
The market was on the defensive from the opening as it made room for the new supply and after U.S. Treasuries weakened on Monday.

The December 10-year bond futures contract dropped through support at 92.520 late in the day after breaking 92.560 soon after opening, ending the day testing 92.500, or the 7.50 percent yield level on the benchmark 10-year bond.
The short-end of the market also weakened, but largely continued to price in a 50 basis point easing in official 7.0 interest rates by the end of the year.
The December bill futures contract closed at 93.50, indicating a 6.50 percent cash rate at maturity.
The local market underperformed other dollar bloc bonds with the Australian/U.S. 10-year yield spread widening to its highest level in almost a week.
September balance of payments are due on Wednesday, which is forecast to show a A$1.3 billion current account deficit.
